Subject: Pilot model recommendations & initial constraints

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — helpful session. Quick recap of our constraints so the pilot recommendations can be targeted: 

- Production target: ~10k interactive queries/day to start, expected to scale to 50k within 6 months.
- Latency SLO: median <120ms for short queries (~20 tokens), 95th <350ms for mixed traffic.
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep inference spend under $5k/month during pilot (excluding infra setup).
- Quality: precision on entity extraction and concise summaries is the highest priority; hallucination tolerance very low.

We're keen on a two-track pilot: (A) a fast, lower-cost baseline we can iterate against, and (B) a higher-quality variant for riskier user-facing flows. Can you propose a compact slate (2–4 models) with bench highlights, prompt set links, and the failure modes we should watch for? Also note any operational guards (KV caching, quantization recommendations, canary routing) that matter.

Evan
Evan Clark
Senior PM, AltaData

Hi Evan / Priya — thanks for the clear constraints. Attached is a concise recommendation pack; below is the 3-model slate we believe balances your latency/cost/quality goals and a short rationale for each. Also flagged are the key regression risks and an ops checklist for the staging run.

Recommended slate (purpose-built):

1) rdw-lite-4b-q8 (baseline) — purpose: low-cost, low-latency baseline for high volume endpoints.
   - Pros: ~2x cheaper than 13B-class; median latency measured at ~85ms on our dedicated pool for 20-token queries (P50).
   - Cons: loses subtle entity disambiguation on long context; hallucination rate measured ~6% on our entity extraction eval set.

2) mistral-edge-7b (balanced) — purpose: better quality without large latency hit.
   - Pros: stronger factual recall and cleaner summaries; P95 ~240ms on mixed-length traffic; hallucination ~3%.
   - Cons: cost ~1.8x baseline.

3) rdw-13b-quant (quality variant) — purpose: high-quality production variant for critical flows.
   - Pros: best precision on entity extraction and summarization; hallucination <1.5% on our eval set.
   - Cons: P95 ~410ms in single-GPU config — recommend autoscaled dedicated pool or batching with reserved capacity.

Quick ops and regression guards:
- Default: start with rdw-lite-4b-q8 behind a 10% traffic canary to mistral-edge-7b for 2 weeks. If quality regression (entity F1 drop >3 pts) observed, route critical flows to rdw-13b-quant.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated query roots (noticeable token savings on conversational prefixes).
- Quantization: keep 13B in q4_0 for best quality/cost mix; rdw-lite uses q8 by default.
- Prompt sets: attached prompt_sets_v1.jsonl — includes entity extraction and summary prompts plus guardrails (source attribution, response-length caps).

Attachments: pilot_reco_pack.pdf (full rationale), benchmarks_20271205.csv (raw run results), prompt_sets_v1.jsonl (prompt examples). Drive link included in the attachments section.

High-level cost estimate (pilot, rough):
- Baseline (rdw-lite-4b-q8) at 10k queries/day: ~$1,100/mo (inference tokens only)
- Balanced (mistral-edge-7b) for 10% canary traffic: incremental ~$220/mo
- Quality (rdw-13b-quant) used for 5% critical flows: incremental ~$450/mo
-> Expected total ~ $1.8k/mo during pilot — comfortably under your $5k threshold with headroom for scaling. Numbers are conservative and exclude infra setup and reserved capacity discounts.

I'll let Marissa add the live benchmark pointers and per-model SLA implications. Happy to hop on a quick alignment call if helpful.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Adding the benchmark excerpt and a brief ops note — pulled from the 2027-12-04 run against your representative prompt set. Raw CSV attached (benchmarks_20271205.csv).

Bench highlights (median / p95 / cost-per-1M-tokens):
- rdw-lite-4b-q8:  median 85ms / p95 180ms / ~$420 per 1M tokens
- mistral-edge-7b: median 120ms / p95 240ms / ~$760 per 1M tokens
- rdw-13b-quant: median 220ms / p95 410ms / ~$1,600 per 1M tokens

Regression note: our entity extraction eval (2.4k labeled queries) flags the following failure modes to watch for in early telemetry: 
- Context truncation when prompt+user history approach 1k tokens (use KV caching and shorter prompt windows).
- Length inflations: some templates induce verbose summaries; add response-length caps in instruction layer.
- Prompt sensitivity: rdw-lite shows higher variance when prompts are nominally re-ordered — enforce canonical prompt templates in the client.

Ops recommendations specific to your infra: 
- Start on Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity of a single 8-GPU pool for the 13B variant to keep p95 predictable; use hosted for the baseline to reduce setup time.
- Configure per-model tracing and token-level cost alerts; add a quality monitor that computes entity-F1 daily vs. the seed eval set and emits regression alerts when delta<= -2.5 pts.
- Canary schedule: 10% -> 25% over 72 hours if no regression, with automatic rollback to baseline if entity-F1 drops by >3 pts or latency SLO breaches.

I've added the Drive link to the benchmark artifacts and the prompt set.

Marissa Cole
Senior Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
